title: Data retention and use for training

opening.headline: Learn how to check how much data entered into AI is kept and used for model training by dividing it into retention, training use, and abuse monitoring.
body: Imagine an employee pasting a customer contract into AI and requesting a summary. Where will that conversation remain for several days? Will it be used for model training? The answer depends on whether you have a personal app, a business plan, or an API, and your account settings.

In this lesson, we'll first see that service logs, learning usage, and abuse monitoring archives are different things. Next, we compare the conditions of Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google in the same framework, and look at the conditions and exceptions for no retention (ZDR), and the reading order in cases where settings overlap when an organization sets a retention period.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain differences in retention and learning usage conditions by consumer, enterprise, and API product family
Can distinguish between no-preservation conditions and exceptions

screens.title: How long is the entered data stored and used for learning?
screens.lead: Read a common scene and find out what questions are difficult to answer.

visual.alt: A scene showing the employee screen pasting a contract into AI and the three paths of personal app, corporate plan, and API with question marks.

paragraphs: An employee pastes the text of a customer contract into AI and asks for a summary. This is a common occurrence at work. But not many people know where this conversation lasts and for how long.

The same applies to whether it is used for model training. There is no one-size-fits-all answer because it depends on the type and settings of your account. Personal apps, enterprise plans, and APIs have different terms and conditions. This applies even to products from the same company.

There are three concepts here that are easy to mix up. It's a short archive that the product saves to display conversations, whether it's used to improve models, or to look for policy violations. If you lump these three together, you may misunderstand the statement that it is not used for learning as meaning that it is not even saved.
The questions for this class are: What items should be checked for retention period and learning use?

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: When you read the sentence about not using it for learning, what should you check next? Answer this question again at the end of class.

screens.outro: First, let me recall an experience where I had a similar question.

screens.title: Think of a similar situation
screens.lead: If you think about the question on your own first and then select it, the instructor will organize it for you. You will not enter or submit an answer.

items.prompt: Have you ever wondered if your AI conversation history was really deleted when you deleted it?
items.answer: Disappearing from the list on the screen and actually being erased from storage are two different times. Provider documentation often states that it disappears immediately from the screen and is deleted from the backend within a certain period of time. When talking about deletion, we need to separate the user screen and the backend.

items.prompt: Do you remember seeing settings phrases like ‘Used to improve model’?
items.answer: This phrase is a setting that determines whether the conversation can be used as training data. It matters whether the default is on or off, and whether it varies depending on the account type. In personal apps, it is set by the user, and in corporate products, it is often stated that it is not used for learning by default.

items.prompt: Has your company's security policy ever asked how long your AI service will retain data?
items.answer: This is one of the first questions security personnel ask. The answer needed at this time is not a single number, but a table divided by product group and item. The goal of this class is to be able to fill out just such a table.

screens.outro: Now let's start by distinguishing between the three different items.

screens.title: Three divisions: archiving service logs, learning usage, and abuse monitoring
screens.lead: Select the three tabs one by one to distinguish between three seemingly similar but independent items. The final tab outlines how to read together.

tabs.label: service log
tabs.body:
**Service logs** are records that the product saves to display and continue conversations. This includes a list of conversation history and content stored in the project. This record allows users to continue yesterday's conversation today.

Retention periods vary by product family and settings. When a user deletes an item, it disappears from the screen, but it may take a separate period of time before it is removed from storage.

tabs.label: learning use
tabs.body:
**Training Enabled** is whether the saved data is used to improve the model. It is determined by separate settings and terms. In personal apps, users can directly turn model improvement settings on or off, while enterprise apps or APIs often do not use them for training by default due to separate commitments.

Not using it for training just means not putting it in the learning pipeline, it doesn't mean there are no service logs or abuse monitoring records.

tabs.label: Abuse Monitoring Storage
tabs.body:
**Abuse Monitoring Archives** are short records kept to detect policy violations. Learning and purpose are different. The Gemini API document explains that abuse monitoring logs are used only for policy enforcement and are not used for learning models other than those for policy enforcement.

Therefore, even if you do not learn it, it may be stored for a certain period of time due to abuse monitoring. How long we keep these records depends on your provider and account type.

tabs.label: read together
tabs.body:
The three items are independent of each other. So not learning does not mean not saving.

When reading a document, create a separate column for each item and check it. **How ​​much service logs are left, are they used for learning, and how long are they kept for abuse monitoring?** The period figures vary depending on the provider and account type, so you must check each item.

screens.outro: Now, let’s look at the conditions for each product line of Anthropic in a table.

screens.title: Why Using Learning Is Dangerous: The Difference Between Input and Learning
screens.lead: Select the two states alternately and compare what changes when the same data is used as input for inference and when used for learning. Confirm only the extent of known facts without exaggeration.

states.label: When used as input for inference
states.body:
A model uses input only while it is taking input and calculating a response. The numbers determined through training, i.e. the model's weights, do not change during this process. After a conversation ends, all that remains are the records saved by the service, and those records are managed by retention periods and deletion policies.

So the risk in this case boils down to how long the stored records last and to whom they are visible. When a deletion request is made, you can respond by finding the storage and deleting it. This includes the service logs and abuse monitoring archives identified earlier.

states.label: When used for learning
states.body:
As data is used for training, it is reflected in adjusting the model's weights. Because the original text is not stored in one place like a file, but scattered throughout the model, it is difficult to select and delete only one person's information.

Additionally, research has reported that large-scale language models can be induced to release part of their training data as is. Carlini et al.'s study restored hundreds of raw text sequences from queries in GPT-2, including sentences that appeared only once in the training documents, and reported that the larger the model, the more vulnerable it was. This does not mean that any model can easily reproduce the training data, but rather that it has been proven that reproduction is possible.

Regarding whether personal information can be viewed anonymously in models used for learning, the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) is of the position that it cannot automatically be considered anonymous and must be judged on a case-by-case basis. Therefore, the use of learning is an item that must be checked separately from log preservation, and the moment it is used for learning, it may become difficult to respond to access and deletion requests on an individual basis.

screens.outro: Now that you know why learning usage is a separate check, let’s compare Anthropic’s terms and conditions for each product line in a table.

ext.title: Carlini et al., Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
EDPB, Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models

screens.title: Anthropic’s Consumer, Enterprise, and API Terms
screens.lead: Read the table from top to bottom to see how conditions differ depending on the product line even within the same company.

If classified as a usage policy violation, input and output may be kept for up to 2 years, and classification results may be kept for up to 7 years.
Save and continue products preserve conversations within the product. Some products allow organizations to set retention periods.
If classified as a usage policy violation, input and output may be kept for up to 2 years, and classification results may be kept for up to 7 years.
The developer documentation explains that conversations are not preserved by default. The privacy information states that input and output are deleted from the backend within 30 days.
We promise that the preserved data will not be used for model training without your explicit permission.

data.notes: Even for the same company, the conditions for consumers, businesses, and APIs are different. Content sent through the Feedback button may be stored separately for up to 5 years. The Model Improvement setting applies to new or restarted conversations after you turn it on, and is not retroactive to conversations that have already passed. The numbers in the table are the values ​​written in the provider's documentation, and the API's retention description should be read together with the developer documentation and privacy information, as they are written from different perspectives.

screens.outro: Next, let's compare OpenAI and Google's terms side by side.

screens.title: OpenAI and Google's retention terms
screens.lead: Compare the retention conditions of OpenAI and Google by switching between the two states. Notice how the default retention period differs from the exception approval method.

states.label: OpenAI
states.body:
**OpenAI API** generates abuse monitoring logs for all API functions and is kept for up to 30 days by default. Exceptions are made when longer retention is required by law or is reasonably necessary. Authorized customers may select **Modified Abuse Monitoring** or **Zero Data Retention**, which excludes Customer Content from these logs.

**OpenAI corporate product** basically states that it does not use business data for model training, and informs that it has completed SOC 2 audit. If the user explicitly chooses to share it, such as through feedback, it can be used to improve it. That is, the default is Do not use for training, and exceptions are explicitly selected by the user. Another thing to note is that even if you are approved for ZDR, certain models or features may not be eligible.

states.label: Google
states.body:
Logs for projects with billing settings in **Gemini API** are kept for up to 55 days by default, and can be changed to 7 days, 14 days, 28 days, or 55 days. There is no separate retention period for logs created from datasets, and sharing datasets with Google can be used for product improvement and learning, so we advise you not to include personal, sensitive, or confidential information.

**Google Cloud** promises to restrict training by not training or fine-tuning models with customer data without prior permission. Aside from this promise, saving happens when you turn on features like request response logging. So, promising not to spend anything on training and not saving anything are two different things. Google's two products also have different conditions in that Gemini API is for developers and Google Cloud is for enterprises.

screens.outro: Now let's look at the conditions and exceptions for the most stringent condition, zero retention (ZDR).

screens.title: Conditions and exceptions to no-retention (ZDR)
screens.lead: The following flashcards explain the no-retention terms and common precautions of the three providers. When you select a card, it flips over and you can move to the next card with the right arrow.

cards.back: We do not store the customer's prompts and responses after returning the API response. ZDR is activated separately for each organization, and activation in one organization does not automatically apply to other organizations. Console, consumer, Teams, and Enterprise product screens are not eligible.

Customer content is excluded from abuse monitoring logs, and the store parameter is always treated as false even if the request sets it to true. Features that require approval and are listed in the table as not eligible for ZDR can save their application state even when ZDR is turned on.

If the customer does not turn on request response logging, the Interactions API requires zone-specific action, such as specifying store=false. This is because some functions have a default value of Save. Request response logging is off by default, but when turned on, requests and responses for a specific model are logged to the BigQuery table you specify. You can understand it as a list that must be checked in each area, rather than a switch that can be set all at once.

cards.front: Save that can't be turned off
cards.back: There are some features, such as Google Maps justification, that you cannot turn off 30-day storage. Some of Anthropic's Covered Models require 30-day retention and cannot be used as ZDR without separate approval. Even if you have ZDR, you need to check whether the function you want to use is in an exception.

Even in ZDR, the state can be saved depending on the function. So, don't judge by just looking at the product name, but check the application table for each function published by the provider. Before introduction, find the functions you want to use one by one in the table and record whether or not they are applied. These records serve as the basis for security reviews.

screens.outro: We'll also look at hold rules and the ability for organizations to set their own retention periods.

screens.title: Custom retention settings, log policies, Vault retention
screens.lead: Expand the topic to see three ways your organization administrator can adjust retention.

items.title: Claude Enterprise Custom Retention
items.body: In the Enterprise plan, the Primary Owner or Owner role sets the organization's retention period. The minimum retention period is 30 days and each month is counted as 30 days. The retention period counts from the last activity, and conversations within a project follow the project retention period. The default is to keep it indefinitely unless otherwise specified.

items.title: Project priority rules
items.body: The retention period of a project always takes precedence over the retention period of the conversations within it. If you do not specify a separate period for the project, the project will be kept indefinitely by default, so the conversations within it will not be erased by the organization's conversation retention period. When you move a conversation to a project, it becomes subject to the project's retention period. Conversely, if you move the conversation out of the project, it becomes an independent conversation again and becomes subject to your organization's conversation retention period. A project's retention period is restarted with activities such as adding dialogue or modifying files within the project.

items.title: Google Vault Preservation
items.body: Google Vault applies retention rules and holds to Gemini app conversations. Vault's retention rules and holds take precedence over Admin console settings or user settings, and those settings only hide the conversation from the user's screen. It may take up to 24 hours for the rule to be reflected, and at least 30 days for it to be removed from all Google systems once the deletion rule expires.

items.title: a matter of balance
items.body: Conservation is not an issue where one side is right. It is a balancing act between the need to retain as little personal information as possible against the need for long-term retention for legal obligations or dispute response. Organizations must explicitly determine which data will be retained, for what reason, and for how many days. If not specified, the default value will be used instead. The default for Enterprise is indefinite, so choosing not to decide on it means keeping it for a long time.

screens.outro: Now let's apply the concept to an example. First, medical data.

screens.title: HIPAA, PHI, BAA: Glossary of medical information terms
screens.lead: The following flashcards explain six terms you often encounter when dealing with medical information. When you select a card, it flips over and you can move to the next card with the right arrow. The goal is to help you understand the relationships between terms, even if you're not familiar with medical regulations.

cards.back: This is a federal health information protection regulation in the United States. Restrict how personal health information is used and disclosed and require that it be handled safely. The rules are contained in Parts 160 and 164 of Title 45 of the Code of Federal Regulations. Although it is a U.S. law, services that handle data from U.S. medical institutions are required by customers to meet conditions that meet this regulation.

These are organizations directly subject to HIPAA. These include health insurance plans, health information clearinghouses (organizations that broker claims information, etc.), and health care providers who conduct standard electronic transactions. If a hospital wants to summarize patient consultation records with AI, this is the place for them.

An external organization that performs functions or services related to health information on behalf of a covered organization. Examples include claims processing, data analysis, and legal, accounting, and consulting services. If an external AI service processes PHI on behalf of the hospital, it may be placed in a partner position. This is an assumption and actual judgment will depend on how the Service handles the information.

This is health information that can identify an individual. This relates to past, present, and future physical and mental health, provision of medical care, and payment of medical expenses, and when an individual can be identified through information such as name, address, and date of birth. Regardless of whether it is an electronic document, paper, or oral form. De-identified information is not subject to the restrictions of this rule.

A written agreement between a covered organization and a business partner that sets out the safeguards the business partner will apply to PHI and the scope of permitted use. Partners may not use or disclose PHI in ways not permitted by the Rules. Therefore, the first thing to check when entrusting medical data to an AI provider is whether the product has signed a BAA.

cards.front: The relationship between BAA and conservation
cards.back: They are two different devices. BAA is a contract that establishes responsibility and safeguards, and no-retention is a condition that reduces the exposure area by not storing prompts and responses after answering. Medical data checks for both conditions, as having one does not automatically satisfy the other.

screens.outro: Now that the terminology has been organized, let us explain step by step what conditions are identified in hospital cases.

ext.title: HHS, HIPAA Privacy Rule and related regulations guidance

screens.title: Commentary: Why medical data needs no-retention requirements
screens.lead: The instructor provides a step-by-step explanation of a case where a hospital is trying to use AI to summarize patient consultation records. Use the arrows to move through the steps and follow the conditions to check.

steps.title: situation
steps.body: A hospital is looking to use AI to summarize patient consultation records. Consultation records include patient-identifiable health information, or PHI. Damage when exposed is different from general business documents.

steps.title: Step 1. Medical information requires a dedicated product
steps.body: Organizations that handle PHI need HIPAA-ready products that include BAA and safeguards. Neither consumer products nor typical enterprise setups will meet your requirements. The first confirmation in this process is whether a BAA has been concluded. Organizations that enter into a BAA are those covered by HIPAA, such as health care providers, health insurance plans, health data processors and their affiliates.

steps.title: Step 2. Only use functions in BAA
steps.body: Only functions contained within the BAA should be used to process PHI. Just turning on HIPAA compliance does not mean all features are included in the BAA, and coverage varies by feature. Beta features or some tools may be excluded.

steps.title: Step 3. Reducing retention reduces exposure area.
steps.body: No Preservation reduces the surface area by not storing prompts and responses after they are answered. If nothing is saved, nothing leaks or lingers. This effect is greater for data that cannot be restored once exposed, such as patient information. However, HIPAA response is a separate device that protects PHI by applying broader safeguards such as encryption, access control, and audit logs rather than immediate deletion.

steps.title: Step 4. Not all features are covered
steps.body: Even if there is no preservation, not all functions are eligible. Therefore, before introduction, check the function application table and preservation conditions to see how the function you want to use is classified in both BAA and non-preservation.

screens.outro: This time we will see what order they are read in when there are multiple retention settings.

screens.title: Explanation: Reading order when retention settings overlap
screens.lead: We have summarized the situations in which all three settings are in effect at once in a table. Read the explanations to the right of the code in order to see which setting wins. The notation below is for explanatory purposes only and is not the actual settings screen of the product.

data.code:
[Organization Setup]
  Conversation retention period: 90 days

[Project A]
  Retention period: Not set (default is unlimited)
  Contained conversations: 3 items

[Independent Conversation B]
  Do not participate in the project

[Law Team Hold Rule]
  Status: Active

Reading order
  1. Is the conversation part of the project?
  2. Is there a project retention period?
  3. Are there any hold or preservation rules?
  4. Causes additional delay in actual removal at the deletion time

notes.note: This is the conversation retention period set by your organization. This applies to independent conversations, but for conversations within a project, the project's duration takes precedence. It would be wrong to judge that all conversations will be deleted after 90 days based solely on this value.

If your project has no duration, the default is indefinite, so the three conversations inside will not be cleared by your organization's 90-day setting. This is a classic example of discovering a conversation you didn't know would last long.

Independent conversations outside of a project are subject to your organization's conversation retention period. The retention period counts from your last activity, so the period starts again each time you continue the conversation.

Hold and retention rules take precedence over administrator and user settings. If a rule is hung, data may remain even if the user deletes it while the rule is maintained, and only disappears from the user's screen.

This is the calculation order. Even if the deletion time is set, it may take up to 24 hours for the rules to be reflected and at least 30 days for it to be deleted from the entire system, so the actual removal time is later. Therefore, the day you request deletion and the day your data disappears from all systems should not be counted as the same day.

screens.outro: Lastly, we will explain how to read the policies of the three providers in the same table.

screens.title: Explanation: How to read the three companies' preservation policies in the same table
screens.lead: The instructor explains five questions to organize documents from three providers into the same table. Follow the questions in order using the arrows.

steps.title: Question 1. What is the default retention period?
steps.body: Write down the default retention period for consumers, businesses, and APIs. Even if it is the same provider, each product line is different, so they are not combined into one number. The period during which it is deleted from the backend after deletion is also written. For example, the Anthropic consumer plan has a default maximum of 30 days after deletion, the OpenAI API's abuse monitoring logs have a default maximum of 30 days, and the Gemini API's logs have a default maximum of 55 days. Writing the same units in the same column makes comparison easier.

steps.title: Question 2. Is it used for learning?
steps.body: Write down whether the default value is not used for learning, an opt-in that requires the user to select, or an opt-out that requires a user to select. There are also a few cases where it is used in a separate route, such as for feedback or data set sharing. If you look at the default values, services that are not used for learning will also change if the user chooses to share them.

steps.title: Question 3. How much abuse monitoring is kept and are there any exceptions?
steps.body: Write down the duration of abuse monitoring records that remain separate from learning. Check for a default period, such as OpenAI's 30 days, along with an option to opt out once approved. Make note of the application process and how long it will take, as exceptions often require prior approval.

steps.title: Question 4. What are the no-preservation conditions and exclusion functions?
steps.body: Write down whether it offers no retention and what products and features are excluded. If there are functions that cannot be turned off and the status is saved for each function, write them down in the exception box. If this field is empty, it means you haven't confirmed it yet.

steps.title: Question 5: Can organizational managers make adjustments?
steps.body: Write down whether your organization administrator can change the period or preserve it as a rule. You can view custom retention, project priority rules, and even priorities for retention rules and holds, and compare all three providers in the same table. Once the table is complete, you can see at a glance which column has the most unfavorable conditions, and you can consider whether that column corresponds to the most sensitive input for your work.

screens.outro: Now let's organize the entire class.

screens.title: Key points and reflection
screens.lead: Organizes retention, learning use, abuse monitoring, no retention, and priority rules into one.

paragraphs: Keeping service logs, learning usage, and abuse monitoring are different things. A sentence that is not used for learning does not mean that it will not be saved, so check each item separately. Even within the same company, retention and learning conditions are different for consumers, enterprises, and APIs.

No retention is the most stringent condition, but you should also check for excluded products and feature-specific exceptions. For data with high exposure damage, such as medical, check both BAA and no preservation, and compare whether the function you want to use falls within both conditions.

If holds overlap with your organization's retention settings, project priority rules, or retention rules, they are read in order of priority. The answer to the initial question, what to check after reading the statement that it is not used for learning, is service logs, abuse monitoring archives, product lines, and exclusion functions. Checking these four things will help explain where and how much your initial contract summary request will go down.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Think about which product group and under what conditions the most sensitive input in your work is being processed. Consider whether the conditions have been confirmed in writing and, if not, which items to check first.

misconceptions.myth: If you don't use it for learning, it won't be saved.
misconceptions.fact: Storage of learning, service logs, and abuse monitoring are separate items. Even if it is not used for learning, it can be stored for a certain period of time for policy enforcement.

misconceptions.myth: If you delete it, it immediately disappears from everywhere.
misconceptions.fact: Although it disappears immediately from the user's screen, it takes a while for it to actually be deleted from the backend. If there is a retention rule or hold on it, it will remain longer.

misconceptions.myth: If there is no preservation, all functions do not save data.
misconceptions.fact: There are exceptions for non-preservation products and functions. Some features have saves that can't be turned off, so you'll need to check the table for each feature.

misconceptions.myth: The information entered during inference is directly reflected in the model weight.
misconceptions.fact: The input of the inference is only used to calculate the response and does not change the weights. The weights are reflected when the data is used for training. So we check separately whether learning is being used or not.

points: Retention, learning, and abuse monitoring are checked separately.

For No-Retention, read the exclusions table for excluded products and features.
Overlapping settings are read in priority order.
